$ xref match

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com
On this page

Counterpart of each function in another build of the binary, scored by shared locations, strings, immediates and call graph.

Matches stripped functions between two builds (68aa57b vs v0.0.2 / e6037d0) by structural invariants and diffs normalized pseudo-C without address noise.

Usage

xref match [OPTIONS] --other <OTHER> <ADDRS>...

Arguments and options

Arguments

<ADDRS>...
Functions in this binary to match (addresses or symbol names).

Options

--other <OTHER>
The other build of the binary to search for counterparts.
--top <TOP>
Number of candidates shown, 1..=128.
default 5
--ambiguity-ratio <AMBIGUITY_RATIO>
Runner-up / best structural score ratio triggering ambiguity (not a probability).
default 0.95
--diff
Compare bounded plausible candidates by normalized pseudo-C similarity.
--context <QUERY_CALLER> <OTHER_CALLER>
Already matched caller pair: query-side caller followed by other-side caller.
--json
Emit the matches as JSON.

Examples

All examples were recorded on public binaries; see Provenance.

Match --other xref-v0.0.2.stripped ...

Relocates 4 stripped functions from 68aa57b against stripped v0.0.2 despite shifted virtual addresses.

Command
$ xref -b xref.stripped match --other xref-v0.0.2.stripped 0xc7d60 0x9ef60 0xa2270 0xd57c0 --top 2

Reading the output

  • For each queried function: the best counterparts in the other build with their score and its parts (locs shared source locations, strs strings, imms immediates, disps displacements, nbrs call-graph neighbours, size, callees).
  • structural score margin and runner-up ratio say how far the best candidate is ahead; the indented lines list evidence present on only one side.
  • warning: lines state that scores are heuristics and when the candidate list was capped.

Limits

  • Scores are heuristics, not probabilities; a small margin means several plausible counterparts. Confirm with diff-c.

Provenance

Recorded with a development build of xref after 0.4.0 on Linux x86-64, on xref.stripped = a stripped xref build (the binary of the home-page examples); xref-v0.0.2.stripped = stripped xref 0.0.2. Output is unchanged except that whitespace at the end of each line and empty lines at the end of the output are removed; long outputs are cut where marked.
